facts.text: Still Pond was the first Maryland town where women earned the right to vote, a milestone in the state's civil‑rights history.
The town sits at a historic crossroads of MD 292 and MD 566, forming a five‑point intersection that anchors its rural character.
The Still Pond Historic District contains about 75 buildings from the early 19th to 1930s, showcasing Victorian, Colonial Revival, and Craftsman styles.
Preservation efforts aim to maintain the village’s rural charm, encouraging restoration of historic properties and sharing best practices with the community.
The district’s visual unity comes from buildings that face the roads, with older homes close to the street and larger houses set back.
A former post office, warehouse, and Odd Fellows Hall now stand as reminders of Still Pond’s past as a commercial hub on Maryland’s Upper Eastern Shore.
